subject: DeepFin reserved throughput depletion causing timeouts — exec alignment requested
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@deepfin.com>, support@deepfin.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Apr 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: DeepFin reserved throughput depletion causing timeouts — exec alignment requested

Maria / DeepFin support team —

Quick summary: over the last 45 minutes we've observed a sustained depletion of the reserved throughput bucket tied to your Dedicated pool (pool-id: df-prod-82). Symptoms: median p95 latency rising from ~120ms to ~1.8s for text-generation endpoints, intermittent 502/504s for high-concurrency inference, and a drop in effective throughput despite matching request rates. Our monitoring shows token-queueing on the pool and eviction-based fallback kicking in for a portion of traffic.

We pulled early traces and an MRT export (attached) — there are repeated KV-cache misses combined with long kernel saturation windows on a subset of GPUs. This is affecting your production traffic and we need to move quickly.

Immediate asks:
- Can you confirm whether you pushed a large model rollout or traffic spike from any campaign in the last hour? (we see a burst of longer sequences from /v1/generate sessions)
- Grant us permission to provision a temporary capacity uplift to the Dedicated pool for the next 2 hours (we'll track usage and revert).
- Please share any internal error IDs or recent deploy SHAs if applicable.

Attachments: deepfin_mrt_2026-03-31.csv (token/trace summary), runbook_dedicated_pool.pdf (our fallback playbook). I attached an error snippet we pulled for reference; we may need fuller logs from your side.

I'll loop in SRE and my partner on escalation, but wanted to surface to you first. If we can get permission for a short-term capacity bump we should prevent customer impact while we investigate root cause.

Thanks,
Olga
Manager, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
(415) 555-0183

---

From: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@deepfin.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: support@deepfin.com
Date: Wed, 1 Apr 2026 10:42:13 -0700
Subject: Re: DeepFin reserved throughput depletion causing timeouts — exec alignment requested

Thanks, Olga —

We saw errors in our logs around 09:55 PDT correlating with an automated nightly enrichment job; the job starts grabbing longer context blobs for the next-gen recommendations roll. We're rolling that job now but it does look like it sent sustained longer sequences (avg tokens/request ~3.2x typical). Error IDs from our side: DF-ERR-9043, DF-ERR-9047 (sample attached as deepfin_error_snippet.log).

We appreciate the fast heads-up. Please proceed with the temporary uplift — we prefer you coordinate with the account team before any billing-affecting changes, but DeepFin is OK with a short, audited bump to avoid customer-facing timeouts.

Also attaching a short trace from our side that shows the same timeout windows. We'll keep the enrichment job paused until you confirm stabilization.

—Maria
Senior Engineering Manager, Platform
DeepFin Inc.
maria.gomez@deepfin.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@deepfin.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Apr 2026 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DeepFin reserved throughput depletion causing timeouts — exec alignment requested

Olga / Maria —

Thanks for the details, Maria — helpful to see the enrichment job pattern. Operational plan I'm pushing now (short, prioritized list):

1) Immediate mitigation (0-30m):
   - Approve a temporary +20% reserved capacity uplift for pool df-prod-82 (duration: 2 hours). This will reduce queueing while we validate root cause.
   - Apply per-route throttles for the longer-sequence endpoints (we'll polyfill with 429s on heavy requests to protect p95 targets).

2) Short-term stabilization (30m-3h):
   - Route ~10% of traffic to a compatible quantized model variant (lower memory/KV pressure) as safe fallback.
   - Reduce max sequence length defaults via a temporary policy for the enrichment job if DeepFin can apply the change.

3) Post-mortem + preventive (same day):
   - We'll collect kernel/utilization dumps and match to your MRT; SRE to create incident and attach runbook_dedicated_pool.pdf.
   - Once stable, we'll propose a capacity-sizing adjustment and a scheduled canary for future enrichment rollouts.

Operational asks to DeepFin: confirm uplift approval and whether you can revert/pause the enrichment job (Maria indicated paused). We also need a contact for billing approvals if uplift runs past the 2-hour window.

I'll trigger the SRE incident now and request the uplift queue. Olga, can you take lead on sequencing and post-mortem capture? Vivek, FYI — this may require a short exec note if we push billing credits for the bump.

Marissa
Head of Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 1 Apr 2026 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DeepFin reserved throughput depletion causing timeouts — exec alignment requested

Team —

Thanks for the rapid coordination. Approve Marissa's mitigation plan and the temporary +20% uplift for 2 hours. A couple of exec-level notes:

• Please assemble a two-slide exec summary (impact, mitigation, ask) by 15:30 PT so I can brief Finance and Customer Success leadership. Include expected incremental cost for the uplift and proposed credit window if we elect to absorb some cost.
• Capture the exact incident timeline and affected endpoints (we'll need this for the SLA/renewal conversation).
• If the uplift looks like it will run >2 hours, obtain written approval from DeepFin billing contact (Maria, please advise).

Olga — take lead on the post-mortem and cc me on the incident ticket. Marissa — coordinate the SRE uplift action and fallback routing. Maria — appreciate the pause on the enrichment job; we'll revert routing once metrics are green for 15m.

Vivek
VP, Sales Operations (acting)
Redwood Inference
